items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use the distributive laws

Content:
[MATH: (a+b) \cdot c = a \cdot c+b \cdot c]

Content:
and

Content:
[MATH: a\cdot (b+c) = a \cdot b+a \cdot c]

Content:
to simplify exponential expressions.

Content:
For example, suppose we wish to simplify the expression

Content:
[MATH: \left( 3d^2 e^{5} f + 6e f^3 \right) f^2.]

Content:
First, we apply the distributive law.

Content:
[MATH: 3d^2 e^{5} f \cdot f^2 + 6e f^3 \cdot f^2]

Content:
Next, we combine exponents with like bases. In this case, both terms have multiple factors containing powers of [MATH: f,] so let's group these together using parentheses:
[MATH: 3d^2 e^{5} \left( f \cdot f^2 \right) + 6e \left( f^3 \cdot f^2 \right)]

Content:
Finally, we simplify using the laws of exponents. In this case, we apply the product rule for exponents:
[MATH: 3d^{2}e^{5}f^{1 + 2} + 6ef^{3 + 2}]

Content:
which simplifies to

Content:
[MATH: 3d^2 e^{5} f^3 + 6e f^5.]

Content:
Let's see some more examples.

sections.normalized_html:
First, we rewrite the denominator using negative exponents:

[MATH: \dfrac{p^7 q + p q^3}{p^4} = \left( p^7 q + p q^3 \right) p^{-4}]

Now, we use the distributive law, as shown below:

[MATH: \left( p^7 q + p q^3 \right) p^{-4} = p^7 q \cdot p^{-4} + p q^3 \cdot p^{-4}]

Next, we rewrite the terms by combining the rules of exponents with algebraic expressions:

[MATH: p^{7}q ⋅ p^{− 4} + pq^{3} ⋅ p^{− 4}|= (p^{7} ⋅ p^{− 4})q + (p ⋅ p^{− 4})q^{3}; = p^{7 − 4}q + p^{1 − 4}q^{3}; = p^{3}q + p^{− 3}q^{3}; = p^{3}q + (q^{3})/(p^{3})]

First, we rewrite the denominator using negative exponents:

[MATH: \dfrac{v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u}{v^{7/8}} = \left( v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u \right) v^{-7/8}]

Now, we use the distributive law, as shown below:

[MATH: \left( v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u \right) v^{-7/8} = v^{15/8} u^2 \cdot v^{-7/8} + v^{5/4} u \cdot v^{-7/8}]

[MATH: v^{15/8}u^{2} ⋅ v^{− 7/8} + v^{5/4}u ⋅ v^{− 7/8}|= (v^{15/8} ⋅ v^{− 7/8})u^{2} + (v^{5/4} ⋅ v^{− 7/8})u; = v^{15/8 − 7/8}u^{2} + v^{10/8 − 7/8}u; = v^{8/8}u^{2} + v^{3/8}u; = vu^{2} + v^{3/8}u]

Finally, we write fractional exponents as radicals:

[MATH: v u^2 + v^{3/8} u = v u^2 + u \sqrt[8]{v^3}]

Item 2 — Example: Applying the Distributive Law

Example Prompt:
Simplify the expression [MATH: b^{3/4}\left( b^{5/4} c + b^{1/4} c^2 \right).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we use the distributive law, as shown below:

[MATH: b^{3/4}\left( b^{5/4} c + b^{1/4} c^2 \right) = b^{3/4} \cdot b^{5/4} c + b^{3/4} \cdot b^{1/4} c^2]

Now, we rewrite the terms by combining the rules of exponents with algebraic expressions:

[MATH: b^{3/4} ⋅ b^{5/4}c + b^{3/4} ⋅ b^{1/4}c^{2}|= (b^{3/4} ⋅ b^{5/4})c + (b^{3/4} ⋅ b^{1/4})c^{2}; = b^{(3/4 + 5/4)}c + b^{(3/4 + 1/4)}c^{2}; = b^{8/4}c + b^{4/4}c^{2}; = b^{2}c + bc^{2}]

Item 5 — Example: Applying the Distributive Law to Rational Expressions

First, we rewrite the denominator using negative exponents:

[MATH: \dfrac{p^7 q + p q^3}{p^4} = \left( p^7 q + p q^3 \right) p^{-4}]

Now, we use the distributive law, as shown below:

[MATH: \left( p^7 q + p q^3 \right) p^{-4} = p^7 q \cdot p^{-4} + p q^3 \cdot p^{-4}]

Next, we rewrite the terms by combining the rules of exponents with algebraic expressions:

[MATH: p^{7}q ⋅ p^{− 4} + pq^{3} ⋅ p^{− 4}|= (p^{7} ⋅ p^{− 4})q + (p ⋅ p^{− 4})q^{3}; = p^{7 − 4}q + p^{1 − 4}q^{3}; = p^{3}q + p^{− 3}q^{3}; = p^{3}q + (q^{3})/(p^{3})]

Item 8 — Example: Simplifying an Expression Using Radicals

Simplify the expression [MATH: \dfrac{v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u}{v^{7/8}}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we rewrite the denominator using negative exponents:

[MATH: \dfrac{v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u}{v^{7/8}} = \left( v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u \right) v^{-7/8}]

Now, we use the distributive law, as shown below:

[MATH: \left( v^{15/8} u^2 + v^{5/4} u \right) v^{-7/8} = v^{15/8} u^2 \cdot v^{-7/8} + v^{5/4} u \cdot v^{-7/8}]

Next, we rewrite the terms by combining the rules of exponents with algebraic expressions:

[MATH: v^{15/8}u^{2} ⋅ v^{− 7/8} + v^{5/4}u ⋅ v^{− 7/8}|= (v^{15/8} ⋅ v^{− 7/8})u^{2} + (v^{5/4} ⋅ v^{− 7/8})u; = v^{15/8 − 7/8}u^{2} + v^{10/8 − 7/8}u; = v^{8/8}u^{2} + v^{3/8}u; = vu^{2} + v^{3/8}u]

Finally, we write fractional exponents as radicals:

[MATH: v u^2 + v^{3/8} u = v u^2 + u \sqrt[8]{v^3}]
